text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, hiya! Sorry, yeah, I can hear you. Can you hear me? I've got the telly off and everything.
A: Loud and clear. I'm Karen.
B: Gemma. Nice to meet you. Sorry, I'm rubbish at these, I never know what you're meant to say first.
A: Well, nobody does, I don't think. Three minutes with a stranger. It's a bit like speed dating, isn't it, without the wine.
B: Ha, yeah, sort of! I could do with the wine tbh. Erm, did you do the puzzle thing at the start? I was useless at that.
A: I did. I thought half of it was badly worded, if I'm honest. The one with the shapes. I read it three times and I still wasn't sure what they wanted.
B: Oh my God, the shapes one, yeah. I thought it was just me being thick. I just sort of guessed and clicked next.
A: It wasn't you. Whoever wrote it wants a word with themselves. Anyway, where are you based?
B: Catford, South East London. Born and bred, round Lewisham. What about you?
A: Stourbridge. West Midlands, Black Country. Not Birmingham, before you say it.
B: Sorry, I wasn't gonna! I wouldn't know the difference, to be honest, I've hardly been past Watford.
A: Most people don't. It's fine. So what do you do, Gemma?
B: Erm, nothing at the minute, I'm sort of looking. I was at a lettings agency in Lewisham for about eight years, admin and then supervisor, but the branch merged and the hours just didn't work with my daughter's school. She's eight. So I'm looking for something school hours, reception or a school office, something like that.
A: Right. Lettings. So you'll have had the tenants on the phone shouting about boilers.
B: All the time! Every single winter. How did you know that?
A: Because I'm the one they shout at after that. I manage repairs for a housing association. Response times, complaints, contractors not turning up. That sort of thing.
B: Oh no way. I actually live in a housing association flat. Sorry, I'm not gonna complain to you, I promise.
A: Go on, everybody else does.
B: No, honestly, they're alright. It took them six weeks to sort the bathroom extractor fan, but they came in the end.
A: Six weeks for a fan. That'd be a complaint on my desk. I'd be chasing whoever had that job, I can tell you.
B: Ha, I bet you would! You look like you'd sort it. I mean that nicely.
A: I'll take it nicely. My staff would say I'm hard to please, which is probably fair.
B: I was rubbish at that bit when I was supervisor, telling people off. I'd just end up apologising to them. It's awful, I say sorry about everything, do you know what I mean?
A: You've said it about six times already.
B: Have I? Sorry. Oh God, there I go.
A: It's alright. It's better than the ones who never say it. So what do you do when you're not job hunting?
B: Erm, telly mostly, if I'm honest. Gogglebox, Strictly. True crime podcasts, but then I can't sleep and I'm checking the door's locked.
A: I listen to those on the way to work. The traffic on the A491 is that bad I can get through a whole series. And I'll rewatch Gavin and Stacey any day of the week.
B: Oh my God, me too, that's my comfort one. I've seen it about ten times.
A: Nessa's my favourite. She doesn't suffer fools.
B: That's well you, innit. Sorry, I mean, in a good way.
A: Ha. Again with the sorry. No, you're probably right.
B: Do you have kids then?
A: Two. Both grown up now. My son's at university in Leeds and he hasn't rung me in a week, so don't get me started.
